citation: Mattera, S. K., Jacob, R. T., & Morris, P. A. (2018). Strengthening Children's Math Skills with Enhanced Instruction: The Impacts of Making Pre-K Count and High 5s on Kindergarten Outcomes. New York, NY: MDRC.
report_number: MDRC (March 2018) -- Making Pre-K Count / High 5s Impact Final Report (no IES/NCEE number; funded by Robin Hood Early Childhood Research Initiative)
design: RCT; cluster (pre-K site/school) random assignment of the Building Blocks math curriculum + teacher PD/coaching (Making Pre-K Count, MPC) vs business-as-usual; 69 pre-K sites / 173 classrooms in NYC (35 program vs 34 control), 16 random-assignment blocks; subject = early math; grade = Pre-K (treatment delivered in pre-K), outcomes measured at end of kindergarten (spring 2016). Comparison 3 (MPC+High 5s vs no math enrichment) builds on the same cluster-randomized pre-K design within the 47 public-school sites (24 program vs 23 control, of which 22 control sites assessed).
problems: Exact impact standard errors are NOT reported anywhere in the report (only effect sizes and p-values). (1) For each contrast the report gives an effect size d = model-based impact / control-group SD, from a pretest-adjusted two-level (multilevel) model clustered at the pre-K site level, so the reported d is already cluster-adjusted (cluster_adjusted=true) and pretest_adjusted=true. (2) SE was back-solved from the reported two-sided p-value via z = phi^-1(1-p/2): this works for Comparison 1 REMA-K (p=0.11; se_g~0.050, cross-checked against the 90% CI in Appendix Figure E.1 which implies se_d~0.055 -- consistent) and for Comparison 3 WJ Applied Problems (p=0.40; se_g~0.107). (3) SE could NOT be recovered for two effects and is left null: Comparison 1 WJ (d=0.00, p=0.96 -> z~0, indeterminate) and Comparison 3 REMA-K (p reported only as '0.00 ***', i.e. p<0.01, so z is unknown; back-outs range se_g 0.091-0.107 across plausible p, too sensitive to report). For these, n_t/n_c and n_clusters are recorded so the central team can derive variance (the report gives no ICC anywhere -- not guessed). (4) The two registry rows (75, 76) map to the report's two TPD-vs-business-as-usual contrasts: row 75 = Comparison 1 (MPC alone vs pre-K-as-usual), row 76 = Comparison 3 (MPC + High 5s vs pre-K-and-kindergarten-as-usual). The report's Comparison 2 (MPC+High 5s vs MPC only) is NOT a TPD-vs-BAU contrast (both arms received the pre-K TPD/curriculum) and is excluded. (5) Both math outcomes per arm are extracted: REMA-K (researcher/developer-made; developed by the Building Blocks authors) and Woodcock-Johnson Applied Problems (standardized/independent). The report itself notes the REMA-K is NOT closely aligned to the program (only 5 of 48 items overlap; effects robust to removing them). The headline outcome is the REMA-K. Test_type filtering is left to the central merge; the meta-analysis included only independent measures, which would favor the WJ Applied Problems.

effect_sizes.arm_label: Comparison 1: Making Pre-K Count (Building Blocks curriculum + teacher PD/coaching) in pre-K vs pre-K-as-usual (no math enrichment)
effect_sizes.grade_band: Pre-K (treatment); outcomes at end of K
effect_sizes.test_name: Research-Based Early Math Assessment-Kindergarten (REMA-K), T score
effect_sizes.timepoint: post: spring of kindergarten year (one year after the pre-K treatment), spring 2016
effect_sizes.g_method: Report effect size d = impact / control-group SD = 0.08 (Table 3.1; impact 0.73 REMA-K T points, control-group SD back-solved as 0.73/0.08 = 9.1). Hedges g = J*d, df = n_t+n_c-2 = 1323, J = 0.999433, g = 0.07995. SE back-solved from reported two-sided p=0.11: z = 1.598, se_d = 0.08/1.598 = 0.0501, se_g = J*se_d = 0.0500, g_var = se_g^2 = 0.002503. Cross-check: Appendix Figure E.1 (p.72) shows the REMA-K T-score 90% CI ~[-0.005, 0.175], implying se_d ~ 0.055 -- consistent.
effect_sizes.page_ref: Table 3.1 (p.19); Appendix C model (pp.57-58); Appendix Figure E.1 (p.72)
effect_sizes.notes: REMA-K is the report's headline/primary, more sensitive math measure. Positive but not statistically significant overall on the primary T score (p=0.11); logit and raw scoring specifications were significant (ES 0.10-0.12). Impact from a two-level multilevel model (children within sites, sites within blocks) clustered at the pre-K site level, adjusting for pretest and background covariates plus block dummies -> cluster_adjusted=true, pretest_adjusted=true. n_t/n_c are analytic children (Table 3.1); n_clusters = 69 pre-K sites (35 program + 34 control; 16 RA blocks). Means are model-adjusted group means. SDs not reported; the standardizing SD is the control-group SD (~9.1). No ICC reported.

effect_sizes.arm_label: Comparison 1: Making Pre-K Count (Building Blocks curriculum + teacher PD/coaching) in pre-K vs pre-K-as-usual (no math enrichment)
effect_sizes.grade_band: Pre-K (treatment); outcomes at end of K
effect_sizes.test_name: Woodcock-Johnson III Applied Problems subscale, standard score
effect_sizes.timepoint: post: spring of kindergarten year (one year after the pre-K treatment), spring 2016
effect_sizes.g_method: Report effect size d = impact / control-group SD = 0.00 (Table 3.1; impact 0.04 WJ standard-score points). Hedges g = J*d = 0.999433*0.00 = 0.00. SE could not be recovered: with d=0 and p=0.96 the implied z ~ 0, so the SE is indeterminate from the rounded statistics. Left null for central derivation (design-based no-cluster placeholder would be se_d ~ 0.055; ICC not reported, so cannot apply a cluster correction).
effect_sizes.notes: Woodcock-Johnson Applied Problems is the standardized, nationally normed, independent math measure (less sensitive/more global per the report). Essentially zero impact (d=0.00, p=0.96). Same multilevel pretest-adjusted, site-clustered model as the REMA-K row. SDs not reported; standardizing SD is the control-group SD (~15, WJ norm). g_se/g_var null because the SE cannot be back-solved from d=0 with a rounded p=0.96 (see problems).

effect_sizes.arm_label: Comparison 3: Making Pre-K Count (pre-K) + High 5s (kindergarten math-club supplement) vs pre-K-and-kindergarten-as-usual (no math enrichment, public-school sites only)
effect_sizes.grade_band: Pre-K + K (treatment); outcomes at end of K
effect_sizes.test_name: Research-Based Early Math Assessment-Kindergarten (REMA-K), T score
effect_sizes.timepoint: post: spring of kindergarten year (end of the two-year treatment), spring 2016
effect_sizes.g_method: Report effect size d = impact / control-group SD = 0.30 (Table 3.3; impact 2.63 REMA-K T points, control-group SD back-solved as 2.63/0.30 = 8.8). Hedges g = J*d, df = n_t+n_c-2 = 646, J = 0.998839, g = 0.29965. SE left null: the report gives the p-value only as '0.00 ***' (p<0.01), so z cannot be pinned down; back-outs range se_g 0.091 (p=0.001) to 0.107 (p=0.005), too sensitive. n_t/n_c and n_clusters recorded for central variance derivation; no ICC reported (not guessed). Design-based no-cluster reference: se_d ~ 0.079 (would understate variance given site clustering).
effect_sizes.notes: Two years of enhanced math (MPC pre-K curriculum/PD + High 5s K supplement) vs full business-as-usual; this is the largest, statistically significant impact (d=0.30, p<0.01) and the report's headline result (closes >1/4 of the income achievement gap). Cluster-randomized at the pre-K site level: compares children in the 24 MPC program-group public schools vs 23 (22 assessed) MPC control-group public schools; multilevel model clustered at pre-K site, pretest- and covariate-adjusted with block dummies. n_clusters = 46 sites (24 program + 22 assessed control; 11/10 blocks). Means are model-adjusted group means; standardizing SD is the control-group SD (~8.8). g_se/g_var null because exact SE/ICC not reported and p given only as <0.01 (see problems).

effect_sizes.timepoint: post: spring of kindergarten year (end of the two-year treatment), spring 2016
effect_sizes.g_method: Report effect size d = impact / control-group SD = 0.09 (Table 3.3; impact 1.06 WJ standard-score points, control-group SD back-solved as 1.06/0.09 = 11.8). Hedges g = J*d, df = n_t+n_c-2 = 646, J = 0.998839, g = 0.08990. SE back-solved from reported two-sided p=0.40: z = 0.8416, se_d = 0.09/0.8416 = 0.1069, se_g = J*se_d = 0.1068, g_var = se_g^2 = 0.011409.
effect_sizes.notes: Standardized, nationally normed, independent math measure. Positive but not statistically significant (d=0.09, p=0.40). Same site-clustered, pretest-adjusted multilevel model as the Comparison 3 REMA-K row. SDs not reported; standardizing SD is the control-group SD (~11.8). SE recoverable here because p=0.40 is an informative (non-boundary) value.
